doc.tool: Read a Franka state snapshot and its synchronized RGB images.
Read camera intrinsics, crop, depth, and calibration metadata.
Read calibrated camera geometry and projection conventions.

doc.code:
The arm's state: TCP pose (base frame, xyz + quaternion xyzw), joints and gripper width (m).

Example:
    st = get_robot_state()["raw_base_state"]
    print(st["tcp_pose"][:3], st["gripper_position"])

Live RGB-D frames: main_images/main_depths (wrist) and extra_view_* (the other cameras).

Example:
    obs = get_observation()
    wrist, depth = obs["main_images"], obs["main_depths"]  # HxWx3 uint8, HxW m
    scene = obs["extra_view_images"][0]

Camera intrinsics, extrinsics and depth conventions.

Example:
    meta = get_camera_meta()
    for name, cam in meta["cameras"].items():
        print(name, cam["intrinsic_K"])

prompt.description: What to segment, e.g. 'red block' (or give point)

point.description: A positive point [row, col] instead of a prompt

all.description: Return every mask, not only the best (default false)

doc.tool: SAM3 masks on the latest camera image, each with a short id (d3) drawn on the returned overlay in rank order (red, blue, green, yellow, ...). Give exactly one of a text prompt or a positive point [row, col]. all=true returns every candidate instead of only the best; then pick one with select_detection. Ids die with the observation: segment again after any motion.
doc.code:
SAM3 masks on the current observation, each with a short id; all=True returns every candidate instead of the best. Ids die with the next observation.

Example:
    s = segment("red block", camera="third_person")
    if s["found"]:
        print(s["ids"], s["detections"][0]["centroid_rc"])

id.description: A detection id from segment (e.g. d3) of the current observation

doc.tool: Choose one segment mask (by id) as the target of the current observation, after checking the overlay.
doc.code:
Make one detection id the selected mask of the current observation.

Example:
    s = segment("red block", all=True)
    select_detection(s["ids"][1])

id.description: A detection id from segment (e.g. d3) of the current observation

doc.tool: Rule out one segment mask (by id) of the current observation; it stays listed as rejected.
doc.code:
Rule one detection id out; it stays listed as rejected.

Example:
    s = segment("red block", all=True)
    reject_detection(s["ids"][0])

doc.tool: Fill the holes of a camera's depth on the latest step with a UniDepth estimate scaled to the sensor (or supply depth where the camera has none). back_project and segment on this step then use the filled depth; the sensor depth is kept as <camera>_depth_sensor.f32.
doc.code:
Fill the holes of a camera's depth with a UniDepth estimate scaled to the sensor (or supply depth where the camera has none); later segments use the filled depth.

Example:
    r = enhance_depth("wrist")
    print(r)

doc.tool: Back-project one wrist or external-camera pixel into Franka base coordinates.
Fuse matched wrist and external-camera pixels into a Franka base point.

xyz.description: TCP position, base-frame [x, y, z] in m

doc.code:
IK reach check of a base-frame TCP pose from the current joints, nothing moves (--ik): {status: reachable | unreachable | unknown, q, position_err, orientation_err, message}.

Example:
    r = preview_reach([0.5, 0.0, 0.25])
    print(r["status"])

doc.tool: Move the Franka TCP by a bounded base-frame xyz delta in meters (at most {{max_move}} m per call; refused when it ends outside the workspace or below the z floor).
doc.code:
Translate the TCP by a base-frame delta in metres; refused beyond the per-call limit (--max-move) or outside the workspace (--workspace-xy, --z-floor).

Example:
    r = move_delta([0, 0, -0.03])  # 3 cm down; each call stays within the per-call limit
    print(r["ok"], r["final_tcp_pose"][:3])

doc.tool: Rotate the Franka TCP by a bounded base-frame rpy delta in radians (at most {{max_rotate}} rad per call, norm of delta_rpy).
doc.code:
Rotate the TCP by a base-frame roll/pitch/yaw delta in radians; refused beyond the per-call limit (--max-rotate, norm of delta_rpy).

Example:
    rotate_delta([0, 0, 0.2])  # yaw 0.2 rad

Open (open=True) or close the gripper and wait for it to settle.

Example:
    r = set_gripper(False)  # close
    print(r["ok"])

doc.tool: Open the Franka gripper and wait for the command to settle.
doc.code:
Open the gripper fully and wait for it to settle (CaP-X's open_gripper).

Example:
    open_gripper()

doc.tool: Close the Franka gripper and wait for the command to settle.
doc.code:
Close the gripper and wait for it to settle; the fingers stop on an object (CaP-X's close_gripper).

Example:
    close_gripper()

object_name.description: The object in words, e.g. 'red block'

doc.code:
Pose of an object named in words, from SAM3 and depth (CaP-X's get_object_pose): [position (3,), quaternion_wxyz (4,), bbox_extent (3,) or None], in the base frame. The position is the median of the mask's depth points (third-person camera first, then the wrist); the extent the 5th-95th percentile span per base axis. The orientation is identity: disregard it, use sample_grasp_pose's quaternion or the current TCP orientation.

Example:
    pos, quat, ext = get_object_pose("red block", return_bbox_extent=True)
    print(pos, ext)

A TCP grasp pose for an object named in words (CaP-X's sample_grasp_pose): [position (3,), quaternion_wxyz (4,)], base frame. With a grasp server (--contact-graspnet, ...) the best plan_grasp candidate; without one, the object's median depth point with the current TCP orientation (a straight top-down grasp when the gripper points down).

Example:
    pos, quat = sample_grasp_pose("red block")
    goto_pose(pos, quat, z_approach=0.1)

position.description: TCP position, base-frame [x, y, z] in m

z_approach.description: First stop this far back along the gripper's approach axis, m (default 0)

doc.code:
Move the TCP to a base-frame pose (CaP-X's goto_pose): rotate in place to the orientation, then translate to position + z_approach back along the approach axis, then to the position. Every leg is one bounded move_delta / rotate_delta (within --max-move / --max-rotate, the workspace, the floor and the reach check), at most 8 legs per call; the whole route is checked before the arm moves. Returns the last leg's result with legs and reached.

Example:
    pos, quat = sample_grasp_pose("red block")
    goto_pose(pos, quat, z_approach=0.08)
    close_gripper()

Back to the TCP pose of the last reset (CaP-X's home_pose), as goto_pose moves: bounded legs, refused when that takes more than 8 legs.

Example:
    home_pose()

position.description: TCP position, base-frame [x, y, z] in m

doc.code:
The arm's 7 joint angles (rad) for a base-frame TCP pose, by the ik service (--ik) seeded with the current joints; nothing moves. Raises when there is no solution (CaP-X's solve_ik).

Example:
    q = solve_ik([0.5, 0.0, 0.25], [0, 1, 0, 0])

Stream the arm to a joint configuration (Polymetis only; CaP-X's move_to_joints), speed-capped and stop-polled. Refused unless every joint moves at most the server's per-call joint step (limits.max_joint_step_rad), the TCP ends within --max-move and --max-rotate of where it is, and the forward-kinematics path stays in the workspace and above the floor.

Example:
    q = get_robot_state()["raw_base_state"]["arm_joint_position"]
    q[6] += 0.1
    move_to_joints(q)

start_pose_wxyz_xyz.description: Start pose: quaternion wxyz then xyz (base frame)

end_pose_wxyz_xyz.description: End pose: quaternion wxyz then xyz (base frame)

doc.code:
Joint waypoints [N, 7] along a straight TCP line from one pose to another (2 cm steps, orientation slerped, at most 100), each solved by IK from its predecessor; nothing moves (CaP-X's traj_plan).

Example:
    traj = traj_plan([0, 1, 0, 0, 0.5, 0.0, 0.3], [0, 1, 0, 0, 0.5, 0.0, 0.25])
    move_along_trajectory(traj)

move_to_joints through every waypoint in order (Polymetis only; CaP-X's move_along_trajectory): each waypoint is one bounded move_to_joints, and the whole path's TCP travel is at most 8 x --max-move, checked before the arm moves.

Example:
    move_along_trajectory(traj_plan(start, end))

doc.tool: Run bounded real-world VLA action chunks for a local grasp attempt.

waypoints.description: World-frame [x, y, z] positions in m, in order

doc.tool: Move the EEF through 1-5 world-frame positions in order (orientation and gripper held). Checked before anything moves: each segment and the whole route against the per-call limits, each waypoint against the workspace. Stops at the first waypoint not reached. Use it for short routes around an obstacle (lift, carry, descend) instead of one straight move.

point.description: Target pixel [row, col] in the wrist image

row.description: target pixel row in the wrist image

execute.description: Also move by the correction (default false)

doc.tool: Wrist-view alignment near a grasp: give the target's pixel [row, col] in the current wrist image. Returns the lateral EEF correction (in the camera's image plane, at the target's depth, at most max_correction_m) that puts the target under the gripper centre (delta_world) and the EEF position after it (aligned_xyz). execute=true also applies it (move_delta by delta_world; the server enforces its limits); by default nothing moves. Approach depth and orientation are unchanged. The returned wrist image marks the gripper-centre pixel (green) and the target (red).
doc.code:
The lateral EEF correction that puts pixel (row, col) of the current wrist image under the gripper centre (in the camera's image plane, at the target's depth, at most max_correction_m): desired_pixel, target_pixel, delta_world, aligned_xyz. execute=True also moves by it (env.move_delta by delta_world).

Example:
    a = align_wrist(250, 270)
    align_wrist(250, 270, execute=True)

object.description: Without a grasp backend: the object to grasp, e.g. 'black bowl' (required then)

max_candidates.description: With a grasp backend: how many plan_grasp candidates to show (default 8)

doc.tool: A separate vision model's grasp opinion (--grasp-advisor), never moving the robot. With a grasp backend: it sees the latest plan_grasp candidates drawn on the camera image (jaw line, centre dot, approach arrow, one colour each) and recommends the one most likely to hold through lift and carry, or abstains; run the recommended id with execute_grasp (or pass it as grasp_id); call it right after plan_grasp, before the robot moves. Without one: give `object`; it proposes the grasp centre, jaw contacts and top/side approach on the camera image, back-projected to a world grasp (position, approach, eef_yaw, pregrasp_xyz), marked confidence_level low (one image, no width or collision check): approach through pregrasp_xyz and confirm in the wrist view.

point_id.description: a solved mark_point id as the position

approach.description: world direction of the grip frame's +Z

jaw.description: world direction of the jaw axis (+X)

doc.tool: Move the grip site (the point between the finger pads) and orient it, then open or close. Position: at most one of xyz (world m), point_id (a solved mark_point) or delta_mm (delta_frame world = [dX,dY,dZ], grip_site = [dJAW,dLAT,dAPP] along the gripper's current axes); omitted keeps the position. Orientation: approach is the world direction the gripper points along (its +Z; [0,0,-1] = straight down), jaw the world direction the fingers close along (its +X; either sign); give either or both, omitted parts keep the current orientation. preview=true only draws the target (zoomed preview_top/front/side views, markable, and the camera). A close is always previewed first: the result's preview_id, executed unchanged by move_grip({execute_preview_id}) alone while the gripper has not moved; any change needs a new preview. The preview is geometry: it does not predict contact. After a motion: motion_status reached or not_reached (then the gripper is skipped), grip_xyz_m, remaining_delta_mm, rotation_error_deg, gripper_width (closed_on_nothing: no grasp), and in simulation the robot's contacts (cyan on the camera image).
